item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Several minor gripes about this.

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-532 shows a tendency to break down and ingest the dermis, and will not enter the body until the surrounding dermis has been covered.

SCP-532 likes to break down and ingest the dermis. But it will not enter the body until the surrounding dermis has been covered? Also, 'entering the body' can probably be removed considering the next statement is 'SCP-532 will then enter the bloodstream…'

I feel like this sentence is somewhat ambiguous and contradictory, and could be changed to something along the lines of "SCP-532 shows a tendency to break down and ingest dermal tissue before entering the bloodstream."

SCP-532 will then enter the bloodstream, causing major damage to the circulatory system due to the freezing and subsequent crystallization of water molecules. Typically the victim will die of blood loss.

Depending on how fast the bacteria propagates (which isn't directly specified), blood loss would be the least of their concerns. If it's relatively slow to reproduce, then anything infected would likely die due to secondary exposure. Infections are one of the largest concerns in burn wards because you lose your primary protection against pathogens, and many treatment resistant pathogens (not just bacteria) can infect people who lose good chunks of their skin. Not to mention that this thing would inherently cause damage to the immune system simply by being there, weakening defenses further.

If SCP-532 is particularly virulent, then the person probably wouldn't die of blood loss anyways. Organ failure (of some kind) would be more likely, and death from brain damage would be the most likely cause of death as if water in the blood starts to crystallize bad things are going to happen. The brain would probably be the first thing to start to go once SCP-532 hits the bloodstream because of how many small blood vessels there are in the brain. Those blood vessels being damaged (or clotting from pieces of ice getting stuck in them) would start to wreck some serious mayhem very quickly.

Edit: Also "the victim" just doesn't sound very clinical. Not sure exactly what to rephrase it to. Patients, infected individuals…

Upvoted overall because I like the idea behind the SCP.

tl;dr-

Should consider changing

SCP-532 shows a tendency to break down and ingest the dermis, and will not enter the body until the surrounding dermis has been covered. SCP-532 will then enter the bloodstream, causing major damage to the circulatory system due to the freezing and subsequent crystallization of water molecules. Typically the victim will die of blood loss.

to

SCP-532 shows a tendency to break down and ingest the dermis, and will enter the bloodstream once vascular tissue is exposed. This causes major damage to the circulatory system due to the freezing and subsequent crystallization of water molecules. Typically infected individuals will die of organ failure, catastrophic brain damage, or complications from secondary infection.


Please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Re: If you're desperate to science it up...
item.content:encoded:
I agree. Too much detail is given to the activities of the organism, I think. The reader spends too much time thinking to get scared about it.

As for the "freezing agent" naysayers, how about this:
"Instances of SCP-532 that land on a heat-providing organism will produce a natural freezing agent, causing affected cells to freeze and die. Victims of SCP-532 describe this sensation in a similar manner to the cold produced when any natural snowflake touches human skin. SCP-532 will then break-down the dead cell and reproduce."
changing to this:
"In the event that SCP-532 makes contact with a living organism, it immediately produces a chemical which begins an endothermic reaction with the victim's cells. This simultaneously kills nearby tissue and provides a suitable temperature for SCP-532 to reproduce."

It's just a suggestion, but there's nothing scientifically impossible or silly about endothermic reactions.

If you're including scientific information, please fact-check. There's nothing like being completely thrown from immersion due to sloppy science. Granted, due to the nature of the site, much will remain unexplained — but write that, instead of trying to make up BS.

item.content:encoded: There's also the Cat's Cradle approach - the organism could enable crystallization of water at well above 0ºC, possibly by doping the water with some yet-to-be-identified compound. There once was a microbe that lived in the snow,
It very much loved that nice and blue glow,
The cold would often fell an old beast,
And give this germ a mighty good feast,
But lo and behold,
The snow could not hold,
With summer the ice would meet its defeat,
The microbe could not let itself be so beat,
And so it evolved and twisted its genes,
It would make the nice cold by its own means,
It spread and it fed and its populous grew,
'Til it met a trail it must face anew,
This one little biome was still not enough,
For the world held quite a lot of good stuff,
It spread its cells wide,
To the sky it would glide,
And from there it would find a new feast.

Now in the high sky the germ learned to fly,
But in the warm air the spores often die,
The cells are so weak,
While new hosts they seek,
Until it can land on a man it can eat,
The germ cannot afford to run into heat,
It can then shed its airborne shell,
Extruding its endothermic gel,
Freezing its prey and eating away,
Eventually the target t'will slay.

item.title: Re: On plausibility and other like such as.
item.content:encoded:
GENTLEMEN

It would typically take a snowflake at least a little while to hit the bottom, meaning it would melt or turn to slush in above freezing temperature (as it typically does). If it drops into a hot troposhpere, too bad, so sad, it's dead. A freezing agent is a secreted liquid, meaning the liquid would part from the bacteria as it fell.

The bacteria does not enjoy cold blooded organisms, due to them lacking energy in their outer cells. Also, do you really want to read about a SCP that kills ferns?

The bacteria reproduces at a rate of one reproduction per cell ingested. because it has enough freezing agent to kill more than one cell, it can effectively multiply before dying from the heat of the skin.
